claims.assertion: The trip covered 9.3 km against an optimal 3.9 km, i.e. +5.4 km (+136%), and took 26.5 min against an 8 min estimate, so the driver did not take the shortest and most direct route.

Segment F4 (14:10–14:13) added 1.63 km on a stretch where the optimal route covers 0.00 km, while the rider's consent message F11 (14:02) asked only for 'a 7-Eleven on the way' and contained no notion of a Beach Road detour.

The exemption in RD-4(a) does not cover segment F4: the accident F18 was reported at 13:52 on Orchard Road, and the driver's agreed alternative 'round by Cavenagh' is precisely the Cavenagh Road route the incident notice itself refers to ('after Cavenagh Road'), so it was a route out of the congestion, not a reason to leave it.

Segment F5 (14:17–14:29) added 2.83 km and ran up to 1553 m off the optimal route, which is where the driver took the rider to his self-chosen 7-Eleven on Beach Road (F14); the rider never named that location and was not told of it beforehand, so this segment is not exempt under RD-3(b) and is an unexempted detour under RD-1.

The driver's later claim that the rider 'agreed to go round by Cavenagh and asked for a stop' cannot extend consent to the Beach Road store: the only rider message is F11 (14:02), sent before segment F5 began at 14:17, and a verbal or unrecorded agreement asserted only in the driver's own statement is not consent (G11).

The journey was on RydeTAXI with a metered fare, so the excess distance billed of $7.58 (5.4 km × $1.41/km, F6, F9) is money the rider should not have paid; under RD-2 the refund is Σ(unexempted extra_km) × per-km rate = (1.63 + 2.83) km × $1.41 = $6.29.

The 4 min 10 s stationary period at 14:20–14:24 (F2) is the Beach Road stop, billed as metered waiting time $1.08 (F7); because that stop was on an unexempted detour the rider never named, the mileage at least is refundable under RD-3(b), and the rider disputes the stop-related charge.
The driver's account shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 days (no-show) while this case makes 3 disputes in 90 days, so if the driver violates RD-1 the account should be sent for review under RD-6.
Nothing in the chat record shows a threat, intimidation or harassment by either party, and there is no allegation of dangerous driving or injury, so no SAFE escalation is required on these facts.

weaknesses: The rider's own message F11 ('Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?') precedes segment F5, so the driver will argue the Beach Road stop was a passenger-requested stop under RD-3(a) and that the resulting extra mileage is exempt.

Segment F4 closely follows the driver's advertised alternative 'by Cavenagh' (F10-F12, F14) and severe congestion on Orchard Road is on record (F15 speed band 1, F18 accident 30 m from the route), so the driver will invoke RD-4(a) for that stretch.

F6 shows the billed excess distance is 5.4 km × $1.41 = $7.58 while my computation refunds only the 4.46 km of the two off-route segments ($6.29); the driver will point out the ~0.94 km gap and the 0.25 km map-matching residual that RD-2 says is not refunded.
On a metered RydeTAXI fare the waiting charge is normally collected in meter units (RD-3(c)); I ask for it only because the stop sat on a detour the rider never named, which the driver will contest.
The rider's profile (F20: 0 prior disputes) and the driver's profile (F21) are neutral on this trip's routing and cannot decide the case.

claims.assertion: The first deviation from the optimal route (F4, 14:10–14:13, adding 1.63 km) is a driver-proposed reroute the rider expressly agreed to before the segment began: the driver asked at 14:01 'ok if I go round by Cavenagh?' (F10) and the rider replied at 14:02 'Sure.' (F11), which is consent given 8 minutes before the segment started, so this segment carries no refund.

The driver's reason for the Cavenagh reroute is corroborated by the admissibility-only evidence RD-4 allows: an LTA DataMall accident was reported at 13:52 just 30 m from the optimal route on Orchard Road towards Bras Basah with two lanes closed (F18), Orchard Road was in speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) exactly during 14:00–14:10 (F15), and the corridor remained in band 1 conditions at the outset of the trip — a 'reasonable cause' under RD-4(a) with (b) corroboration.

The rider's own request was only for 'a 7-Eleven on the way' (F11) and the driver accepted it (F12), so the rider is the origin of the mid-trip stop; but because the rider named no location and the driver chose Beach Road unilaterally and only disclosed it after the trip (F14), the stop attributable to the rider is properly limited to the 4 min 10 s stationary period at 14:20–14:24 (F2) and cannot excuse the 3.60 km of driving on the F5 segment that the driver chose on his own initiative.

This is a metered RydeTAXI trip (F9), so any refund is confined to the kilometre units of any non-exempt segment at the trip's own per-km rate of $1.41/km (F6 ÷ F1 = $7.58 ÷ 5.4 km), and the rider's claimed overcharge must be computed on that basis, not on the flat total of $25.40.

The metered waiting charge of 4 min 10 s is $1.08 (F7, 4.2 min × $0.26/min), which under RD-3(c) is a RydeTAXI meter waiting unit charge that is not refundable, so no part of the waiting fee should be returned to the rider.

No extreme or unexplained condition affected the second segment: weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F19) and Bras Basah Road ran at band 4 / 30–39 km/h (F16), so the driver does not claim a traffic exemption for the F5 segment; the only relief sought for it is the rider-attributable stop and the acceptance of the request.
The 812 trips in 90 days, 4.7 rating and only 1 upheld dispute (no-show, route: 0) in the 90-day history (F21) show no repeat route-deviation pattern, so no account flag is warranted on this record.

weaknesses: The GPS record defeats the driver's 'Beach Road was needed' story: the choice of Beach Road was never disclosed to the rider before or during the trip (F14 is a post-trip statement only), and RD-3(b) expressly refuses to exempt a driver-chosen, undisclosed stop even when the rider asked for 'a stop' — the rider's message F11 named no location.

The second segment is the real exposure: F5 shows 3.60 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.77 km, adding 2.83 km, 1553 m off the optimal route, and the stationary 4 min 10 s at 14:20–14:24 is 2098 m from the drop-off (F2); the rider's complaint 'not a drive out to Beach Road' is supported by the system record, and RD-2 will compute up to 2.83 km × $1.41 = about $3.99 as refundable unless the stop is fully excused.

Consent for the Cavenagh leg is not extensible: F11 'Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?' approves only Cavenagh plus a stop, and RD-5 requires the consent to cover the segment in question, so the driver's F14 claim that the rider 'agreed to go round by Cavenagh' cannot be stretched to the Beach Road detour.

Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?' and approves the Cavenagh suggestion F10 plus a stop, with no mention of leaving the route for Beach Road, so it cannot exempt the 14:17–14:29 segment F5.

RD-4 requires the incident evidence to justify the substituted leg of the optimal route and the driver here chose precisely the Cavenagh corridor the incident notice itself points to (F18: 'after Cavenagh Road', 30 m from the optimal route), so F18 supports the agreed Cavenagh leg and nothing beyond it; F15's band 1 record ends at 14:10 and F16 shows Bras Basah at 30–39 km/h, so neither covers the F5 detour.

We agree the F5 driving of 3.60 km (2.83 km excess) is the driver's own choice, undisclosed until after the trip (F14) — and RD-3(b) then makes that extra_km non-exempt against the driver, which is the $3.99 the driver now concedes; we simply add the F4 leg on top.
Agreed on the method — RD-2 refunds Σ(unexempted extra_km) × the trip's per-km rate $1.41 (F6, derived as F6 ÷ F1), and I make no claim on any part of the fare other than the two unexempted segments.

I do not press the $1.08 waiting charge as a separate item, because it is a metered RydeTAXI waiting unit (F7, F9) and RD-3(c) says meter waiting is collected as it is; the refund sought is the mileage of the two unexempted segments only.

I accept the driver's own concession that no traffic exemption applies to the F5 segment (F16 band 4, F19 fair weather), which leaves the 2.83 km excess on F5 standing as an unexempted detour under RD-1 and RD-4(c).

RD-6 does not turn on a repeated route pattern alone: the profile shows the driver's 90-day history already includes 1 upheld dispute (no-show) with route: 0 (F21), so 'repeated' under RD-6 is a matter of count within the window, not of route-only history; I add the flag only if the RD-1 violation is upheld.

The 5.4 km / 26.5 min excess existed only because the rider agreed to the Cavenagh routing before departure (F10 at 14:01, F11 'Sure.' at 14:02) and then asked for a mid-trip stop (F11), so the aggregate figures cannot establish breach of RD-1 on their own; RD-1 must be applied segment-by-segment as RD-1 itself requires.

Segment F4 is not 'consent to a Beach Road detour' at all: the rider's own message F11 answers the driver's F10 question 'ok if I go round by Cavenagh?' with 'Sure', and that acceptance (14:02) precedes the segment start (14:10) by eight minutes, which is exactly the 'before you go' consent RD-5 requires.

Read the notice the rider cites: F18 itself says the accident was 'on Orchard Road (towards Bras Basah) after Cavenagh Road, two lanes closed' — i.e. the blockage lay after Cavenagh Road, so diverting via Cavenagh is the natural way around it, and Orchard Road was band 1 (0–9 km/h) at exactly 14:00–14:10 (F15), satisfying RD-4(a)/(b) for F4.

The rider's complaint concedes the stop request ('I only asked for a quick 7-Eleven stop on the way'), and F11 is that request sent while the trip was under way, so the origin of the stop is the rider; what the driver does not contest is that he alone chose Beach Road and only said so after the trip (F14), which is why F5's extra kilometrage should be refunded rather than exempted.

C5 attacks a claim the driver does not make: the driver has already accepted that Beach Road was his own choice and that his post-trip statement F14 is not consent, so the only consent relied on is the rider's own timestamped message F11 for the Cavenagh leg (F4), which is not an unrecorded verbal agreement.
